notes.value:
apr may june seasonal

Wash hands
Wash Noni fruit and place in food grade plastic container to the top.
Close the lid (Fresh air is excluded from these containers, and contact between the juice and fresh air is minimized throughout the process)
The noni juice collects inside the containers and ferments as it gradually seeps and sweats from the fruits. The juice appearance is initially an amber or golden colored liquid that gradually darkens with age.
After 1 month check. can extract witin 1 -2 months.
After approximately 2 months, most of the noni juice separates naturally from the fruit pulp and may be drained from the container and filtered. Use a mesh or cheese cloth to pour the juice into another food grade plastic container then into a bottle.


Therefore, using this method, 100 pounds of fruit may yield about 40-50 pounds of juice, or about 4.5 to 5.0 gallons of juice.

Leftover pulp. After all of the noni juice is drained from the collection and fermentation vessel, the residual pulp may be pressed to express the remaining juice fluids. The leftover pulp and seeds may be used as fertilzer.

Fully ripe fruits contain and release more juice than do under-ripe fruits. The most efficient noni juice extraction by weight is obtained when ripe, soft, translucent fruits are placed into the juice collection vessels. When green or hard noni fruits are placed into a juice collection vessel, the fruits release significantly less juice than soft, ripened fruits. Furthermore, a light-colored juice product is obtained from fully ripe, translucent fruits as opposed to the significantly darker-colored juice that is obtained when unripe or green fruits are placed into juice collection vessels.
